code:
SELECT lot_id, qty,
  CASE WHEN qty >= 300 THEN 'large'
       WHEN qty >= 150 THEN 'medium'
       ELSE 'small' END AS size
FROM lots;
code_spoken: Select lot id, qty, and case when qty is at least 300 then large, when qty is at least 150 then medium, else small, end, as size, from lots.
model_answer_spoken: It labels every lot as large, medium or small by quantity. 300 or more is large, 150 or more is medium, and the rest are small.

code:
SELECT part_name FROM parts
WHERE part_id IN (SELECT part_id FROM lots WHERE qty > 450);
code_spoken: Select part name from parts where part id is in a subquery, select part id from lots where qty is greater than 450.
rubric: the subquery finds parts that had a lot over 450
the outer query lists those parts' names
model_answer_spoken: It lists the parts that have at least one lot with more than 450 units.

prompt_spoken: When would you use a with clause, a common table expression, instead of a subquery?
rubric: the query reads top to bottom
it helps when the result is used more than once
model_answer_spoken: Use a with clause to name an intermediate result so the query reads top to bottom, or when you need the same result more than once. A subquery is fine for a small one-off filter.
